newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican primary Cetes rates seen declining more.
newsitem.headline: Mexican primary Cetes rates seen declining more.

text.p: Mexico's bellwether one-month treasury bill rate is seen continuing its downward slide for the third straight week at the Banco de Mexico auction of Cetes on Tuesday, analysts said on Monday.

News just a few minutes before the close of trade in the secondary market on Monday that Attorney General Antonio Lozano Gracia had been removed from his post came too late to affect the market, but cast a shadow on the outlook for interest rates, dealers said.
The news was likely to pressure rates on Tuesday and check an expected fall in primary rates.

"We estimate new reductions in the rates for the auction this week, showing the biggest declines in the 28-day term, followed by the 91- and 182-day terms," said Banorte in its weekly report released earlier in the day.
Dealers and analysts had said that the yield on the one-month paper could fall between 50 and 80 basis points. The longer-term treasury bills could show a smaller decline, analysts had said.
Last week the rate on the one-month paper fell 77 basis points to yield 29.08 percent.

The move last week by the central bank to ease monetary conditions by moving to a neutral stance in the money markets after leaving the markets short 20 million pesos a day has also helped rates to fall, analysts said.

"The change in the liquidity objective has created a more liquid environment. In the secondary market, there has been good demand, including in the terms most affected by inflationary increases expected in December," said one analyst.
On Monday, the same-day Cetes rate fell slightly to close at 27.80 percent in the secondary market.
The stability in the exchange rate has been a factor helping rates to decline.
Banco de Mexico is offering 3.3 billion pesos worth of Cetes at the auction this week.
